title: AI will replace every compiler engineer by 2028
author: hypecycler

comments.author: ssaform
comments.text: The article is more careful than this title. Its actual claim is that learned heuristics will replace hand-tuned inlining and register allocation cost models, which is already happening in a few production compilers.

replies.author: hypecycler
replies.text: The title is the article's conclusion, stated plainly. I would rather keep it than soften it.

replies.author: peepholer
replies.text: Cost models are the easy part to learn, because you can measure the result. Correctness is the part nobody wants to hand to a model, and that is most of the job.

replies.author: ssaform
replies.text: Agreed. A heuristic that picks a bad inlining decision costs you speed. A pass that miscompiles costs you a week of someone's life.

comments.author: kernelpanda
comments.text: Every decade has one of these. The optimiser gets smarter, the people who understand it get more valuable, not less.

comments.author: regalloc
comments.text: The benchmark numbers in section three are on a suite the authors also trained on. I would wait for results on something held out before drawing conclusions.

replies.author: hypecycler
replies.text: The appendix has a held-out run. Smaller gains, same direction.
